2609.04494.title: Hakken: Predicting future discoveries to fill the gaps in today's knowledge
2609.04494.paper_summary: We present Hakken, a domain-agnostic prediction and explanation system performing knowledge prediction, i.e., growing scientific knowledge by establishing novel relationships, ones that are not limited to the deductive hull of previous knowledge. Hakken uses a transformer-based prediction model built on temporal sequences of knowledge graphs extracted from vast bodies of research publications, fused with an LLM's semantic knowledge, to predict the presence and define the type of as-yet undocumented relationships between scientific concepts. It then calls a model-agnostic explanation framework to provide accompanying information for each prediction that allows scientists to evaluate the suggested new relationship. While general purpose, we demonstrate Hakken's practical capabilities by applying it to the biomedical domain. There, Hakken's prediction model establishes a new benchmark for time-aware multi-label relation prediction, and we show that the model's output stays coherent and informative over extended time spans in historic data. In addition, we scored 1.5 million above-confidence-threshold hypotheses related to aging, qualitatively validated batches of these predictions with biologists and progressed three of them for empirical validation in wet-lab. Two predictions with potentially significant impact in the context of drug discovery and repurposing were confirmed, introducing previously undocumented interactions between TP53 and BAMBI, and between RAF1 and TNF, to biomedical science.
2609.04494.paper_summary_zh: 我們介紹 Hakken，一個領域無關的預測和解釋系統，執行知識預測，即通過建立新關係來增長科學知識，這些關係不僅限於先前知識的演繹外殼。 Hakken 使用基於Transformer的預測模型，該模型建立在從大量研究出版物中提取的知識圖譜的時間序列上，並與 LLM 的語義知識融合，以預測科學概念之間尚未記錄的關係的存在並定義其類型。 然後，它調用一個模型無關的解釋框架，為每個預測提供附加信息，讓科學家評估建議的新關係。 雖然是通用的，但我們通過將 Hakken 應用於生物醫學領域來展示其實用能力。在那裡，Hakken 的預測模型為時間感知的多標籤關係預測建立了一個新的基準，我們顯示該模型的輸出在歷史數據的延長時間跨度內保持一致且信息豐富。此外，我們對 150 萬個超過信心閾值的與衰老相關的假設進行了評分，並與生物學家質性驗證了這些預測的批次，並將其中三個推進到濕實驗室的實證驗證中。在藥物發現和再利用的背景下，兩個具有潛在重大影響的預測得到了確認，引入了 TP53 和 BAMBI 之間，以及 RAF1 和 TNF 之間的先前未記錄的相互作用，對生物醫學科學。
